trial_court: Learned VI Additional District Judge, Durg District Durg (C.G.) in Civil Appeal No. 00032A/2014
case_name: Smt. Dulari Bai vs Shiv Singh Chouhan

parties.respondent_defendant: Shiv Singh Chouhan and others (7 respondents)

facts_of_case: The parties are disputing ownership of land at Village Murmunda. The plaintiff sought declaration of title and permanent injunction. The trial court allowed the suit, and the defendant appealed.

legal_principles.principle: A Second Appeal lies only on a substantial question of law.
legal_principles.held: Findings of fact concurrently recorded by the courts below are ordinarily final and cannot be interfered with unless such findings are shown to be perverse, based on no evidence, arrived at by misreading of material evidence, or recorded by applying incorrect legal principles.

legal_principles.principle: A court's findings of fact are final and binding unless shown to be perverse or based on no evidence.
legal_principles.held: Findings of fact concurrently recorded by the courts below are ordinarily final and cannot be interfered with unless such findings are shown to be perverse, based on no evidence, arrived at by misreading of material evidence, or recorded by applying incorrect legal principles.

legal_principles.principle: The principle of estoppel applies when there is an admission by one party that can be relied upon by the other.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, on the principle of estoppel, as embodied under Section 114 of the Indian Evidence Act, the plaintiff is not entitled to take a stand contrary to such admission, particularly in respect of title.

outcome.final_order: The impugned judgment and decree dated 16.11.2015 was upheld.
